subject: Health Education
sourceFile: Sciences -- HEALTH EDUCATION OR HEALTH SCIENCE.txt
examFormat: Three papers, all of which must be taken; Papers 1 and 2 form a composite paper taken at one sitting. Paper 1: fifty multiple-choice objective questions, all to be answered in 1 hour for 50 marks. Paper 2 has Section A (six short-structured questions, all answered, 30 marks) and Section B (three essay questions, two answered, 40 marks), lasting 1 hour. Paper 3: a practical test for school candidates and an alternative test of practical work for private candidates, lasting 1 3/4 hours for 80 marks.

topics.name: History and Development of Health Education
topics.content: Students should visit and observe community, health facility and work place based health education programmes and services.

subtopics.name: Meaning and Setting for Health Education
objectives: State the meaning of health education
Describe the settings for health education: home-based, school-based, community-based, health facility-based and work place-based
State the meaning of health promotion

subtopics.name: Cells and Tissues of the Human Body
objectives: Identify the types of cell: somatic cells and sex cells
Describe cell division: mitosis and meiosis, and state the differences between them
Explain cell differentiation: formation of tissues, organs and systems (epithelial, connective and muscular tissue)
Distinguish between growth and development and discuss the factors that affect them
Describe the structure of a typical animal cell and the functions of its parts

subtopics.name: Sense Organs
objectives: Describe the structure and functions of the eye, ear, skin, nose and tongue
Explain accommodation and the process of hearing and balancing

subtopics.name: Skeletal System and Muscles
objectives: Describe the general plan of the axial and appendicular skeleton and identify the types of bones in the mammalian skeleton
State the functions of the skeletal system
Describe the structures and types of joints, with emphasis on the synovial joint
Describe the structures and types of muscle tissue in relation to their functions
Explain movement, with reference to origin and insertion of muscles and the classes of levers

subtopics.name: Circulatory System
objectives: Describe the structure and functions of the heart, and of blood and lymph vessels
State the composition of blood and lymph
Describe blood and lymph circulation (pulmonary and systemic) and the process of blood clotting
Explain blood groups, rhesus factor, haemoglobin and genotype, and their relevance to blood transfusion
Describe diseases and disorders of the circulatory system and their causes: sickle cell anaemia, leukaemia, haemophilia, arteriosclerosis, hypertension, coronary thrombosis and stroke

subtopics.name: Digestive System
objectives: Describe the organs of the digestive system and their functions, including accessory organs
Describe the process of digestion and the role of digestive enzymes, substrates and end-products
Explain absorption, assimilation and metabolism
Describe diseases and disorders of the digestive system and their prevention

subtopics.name: Excretory System
objectives: Describe the structure and functions of the kidney and skin
Describe the process of urine formation

subtopics.name: Respiratory System
objectives: Describe the structure and functions of the respiratory system
Explain the mechanism of breathing, gaseous exchange and tissue/cellular respiration
Describe diseases and disorders of the respiratory system and their control

subtopics.name: Nervous System
objectives: Describe the structure and functions of the components of the nervous system (brain, spinal cord and nerves)
Distinguish between voluntary and involuntary actions and study the reflex arc
Describe diseases and disorders of the nervous system

subtopics.name: Endocrine System
objectives: State the location of the different endocrine glands, the hormones they produce and their functions
Explain the effects of over- and under-secretion of hormones

subtopics.name: Homeostasis
objectives: Explain the physiological factors affecting homeostasis: body temperature, blood sugar level, water balance, electrolyte balance, pH and blood pressure
Explain positive and negative feedback control systems

subtopics.name: Posture and Postural Defects
objectives: Define posture and state the characteristics of correct posture
Determine correct postures in sitting, standing, walking and lifting
Identify types of postural defects: flat foot, scoliosis, kyphosis and lordosis, and their causes
Explain the effects of incorrect posture on physical appearance, and on the position and functions of body organs

topics.name: Personal Health
topics.content: Care of body parts including the teeth, mouth, hair, hands and nails should be discussed. The use of the Snellen chart for vision screening and the roles of the eye specialist should be discussed. Otitis media should be mentioned. The use of tuning fork, audiometer, guitar strings and wrist watch in auditory screening, and sign language, should be mentioned.

subtopics.name: Physical Health and Personal Hygiene
objectives: Explain the meaning and importance of physical health
Describe personal hygiene

subtopics.name: Promotion and Maintenance of Health
objectives: Define the promotion and maintenance of health
Describe the factors and their roles in the maintenance of health

subtopics.name: Health Screening
objectives: Describe eye defects and their corrections: myopia, hypermetropia, astigmatism, presbyopia and squints (cross eye)
Describe auditory defects: conductive impairment and neurosensory impairment
Describe disorders of the skin
Describe the care of the eye, ear and skin

subtopics.name: Dental Health Education
objectives: State the meaning and types of dental health education
Describe the types of human teeth, and the structure and functions of the different types
Describe teeth diseases (dental caries and gingivitis)

topics.name: Community Health
topics.content: Advantages and disadvantages of traditional medicine, awareness campaigns, and both the physical and biological environment should be discussed. Candidates should be able to define epidemiology, vital statistics and population dynamics; the importance and use of health records should be stressed.

subtopics.name: Community Health Services
objectives: Define community health services
Identify the providers: orthodox services (e.g. primary health care) and traditional services (e.g. bone setters, birth attendants)
Describe community efforts in health promotion

subtopics.name: School Health Programme
objectives: Define the school health programme
Describe its components: skill-based health education, healthful school environment, school feeding services, school health and nutrition services, and school, home and community relationship
State the goals and objectives of the school health programme
Describe the linkages for promotion: Health Promoting School (HPS), Child-Friendly School (CFS), Focusing Resources on Effective School Health (FRESH), Life Skills (LS) and Education for All (EFA)

subtopics.name: Family Health
objectives: State the meaning of family health
Describe aspects of family health, including maternal and child health (antenatal care, immunization, oral rehydration therapy, breast feeding and safe motherhood)
Discuss family size and budgeting

subtopics.name: Ageing and Death Education
objectives: Define and describe the features of the elderly
Describe ways of relating with the elderly
Explain the meaning of grief and death
Identify common causes of death

subtopics.name: Epidemiology and Vital Statistics
objectives: Define epidemiology and vital statistics
Describe the components of vital statistics: birth rate, mortality rate and morbidity rate
State the uses of the major components of vital statistics

topics.name: Environmental Health
topics.content: Effects of poor sanitation and pest infestation in the home and of substandard housing on health should be discussed. Sources of water should include rain, borehole, rivers, streams, springs, well, pond and pipe-borne water. Advantages and disadvantages of each waste disposal method should be discussed. The need for health care and rehabilitation and for health insurance schemes should be stressed.

subtopics.name: Housing
objectives: State the criteria for good housing, including siting, ventilation, lighting and sanitation
Identify the components of a standard house

subtopics.name: Water Supply
objectives: Define water supply and identify its sources
Describe the purification and uses of water

subtopics.name: Waste Disposal
objectives: State the meaning of waste disposal
Identify the types of waste: refuse and sewage
Describe methods of waste disposal

subtopics.name: Pollution
objectives: Define pollution and identify its types: air, water, soil and noise
State the meaning and sources of pollutants
Explain the health consequences of pollution

subtopics.name: Industrial Occupation
objectives: State the meaning of industrial occupation
Describe the programmes: industrial health services
Identify occupational hazards

subtopics.name: Pests and Vectors Control
objectives: Define pests and vectors and differentiate between them
Identify the habitats of pests and vectors
Describe their harmful effects and control

topics.name: Nutrition and Food Nutrients
topics.content: Tests for starch, simple and complex sugars, proteins and fats should be carried out. Local examples of sources of food nutrients should be mentioned. Caloric needs in relation to age, occupation and health condition, food deficiency diseases, and factors responsible for unbalanced diet and effects of poor diet should be discussed. Factors influencing food choice include availability, religion, education, age, belief, health condition and cost.

subtopics.name: Nutrition
objectives: Identify the classes, sources and functions of food nutrients
State the caloric value of food nutrients

subtopics.name: Balanced/Adequate Diets
objectives: Define a balanced/adequate diet and classify foods
Identify nutritional problems

subtopics.name: Factors Influencing Feeding Habits and Choice of Foods
objectives: Explain the factors that influence feeding habits and choice of foods

subtopics.name: Water in Nutrition
objectives: Discuss the role of water in relation to nutrition

subtopics.name: Nutritional Processes
objectives: Describe ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation and metabolism, and defecation/ejection

subtopics.name: Beverages
objectives: Define beverages
Identify their types and effects (negative and positive), including the nutritional value of non-alcoholic beverages

subtopics.name: Diet for Different Groups of People
objectives: Describe diets for children, male adolescents, female adolescents, athletes, pregnant women, adults and the aged

subtopics.name: Food Hygiene, Preservation and Storage
objectives: State the meaning and principles of food hygiene, including food handling and cleanliness of utensils and surroundings
Explain the effects of methods of food preparation (washing, boiling, frying, baking, roasting) on nutrients
Describe methods of food preservation: smoking/drying/dehydration, freezing/refrigeration, addition of chemicals/sugar/salt, and bottling/pickling/canning

subtopics.name: First Aid
objectives: State the meaning, aims and principles of first aid
Identify the contents of a first aid kit
Describe first aid for specific emergency conditions: cuts, wounds, bleeding, dislocation, fractures, burns, scalds, shock, asphyxia/suffocation and poisoning
Identify agencies providing first aid services

subtopics.name: Disaster
objectives: Define disaster and identify its types
Describe disaster relief activities

subtopics.name: Accident
objectives: Identify the types and causes of accidents
Describe the prevention of accidents

subtopics.name: Disability and Rehabilitation
objectives: Define disability and rehabilitation
Identify the types of disability and describe their prevention

topics.name: Drug, Alcohol and Tobacco Education
topics.content: Terminologies include drug abuse, drug dependence, drug misuse, drug addiction, self medication, alcoholism and rehabilitation. Ways of taking drugs include oral, injection, inhalation, topical and anal. Prevention of drug abuse should be highlighted.

subtopics.name: Drug Education
objectives: Define terminologies in drug education
Identify classes of drugs commonly abused
Describe the ways of taking drugs into the body
Explain drug abuse and the consequences of self medication

subtopics.name: Behaviour Altering Chemicals
objectives: Identify the components of tobacco and the effects of smoking on health
Explain the effects of alcohol on health
Explain the effects of drugs on health

topics.name: Communicable and Non-Communicable Diseases
topics.content: The life cycle of the pathogen of each disease, and of each worm (with the aid of a chart), should be discussed.

subtopics.name: Diseases
objectives: Explain the meaning and classes of diseases

subtopics.name: Communicable Diseases
objectives: Define and classify communicable diseases
Describe air-borne/respiratory diseases: common cold, measles, whooping cough, poliomyelitis, tuberculosis, cerebro-spinal meningitis and diphtheria
Describe water/food-borne diseases: dysentery, cholera, typhoid fever, schistosomiasis and guinea worm
Describe insect-borne diseases: malaria, yellow fever, trypanosomiasis and filariasis
Describe worm infections: Ascaris lumbricoides (round worm), Taenia solium (tape worm), Ancylostoma duodenale (hook worm) and Dracunculus medinensis (guinea worm)
Describe animal-borne diseases: rabies and leptospirosis
Describe contact diseases: gonorrhoea, syphilis, Tinea pedis (athlete's foot), Tinea capitis (ringworm), leprosy, scabies and AIDS
State the factors necessary for communicable diseases to occur: causative agent, susceptible host and transmission route (environment)

subtopics.name: Non-Communicable Diseases
objectives: Describe deficiency diseases: scurvy, pellagra, rickets, kwashiorkor, anaemia, beriberi, etc.

Describe diseases due to growth in cells, heredity and normal disorders: cancer, diabetes, epilepsy, haemophilia, heart disease, hypertension, ulcer, mental illness, sickle cell, rheumatism, infertility, asthma, albinism, etc.

topics.name: Family Life and Human Sexuality Education
topics.content: Secondary sexual characteristics in boys and girls, the menstrual cycle, sex determination and antenatal care should be discussed. Candidates should observe/study the parts of the reproductive organs in a mammal. Causes of infertility should be discussed; artificial insemination and test tube babies should be explained. The meaning of sexuality, sexuality education, sexual reproductive health rights, gender and equality should be discussed. Candidates should be able to distinguish between family planning and safe motherhood, and between population and census; the advantages of an accurate census should be discussed.

subtopics.name: Human Reproduction
objectives: Define reproduction, sex gametes, ovulation, menstruation, fertilization, pregnancy and gestation
Describe the structures and functions of the male and female reproductive organs
Describe conception, pregnancy, foetal development and child birth
Describe diseases and disorders of the reproductive system

subtopics.name: Human Sexuality Education
objectives: State the meaning and importance of human sexuality education
Describe life skills (assertive negotiation and communication skills)

subtopics.name: Family and Family Member Roles
objectives: Define the family and identify its types
Discuss family size

subtopics.name: Family Life Challenges
objectives: Discuss family life challenges: widowhood, single parenthood, pre-marital and extra-marital affairs, in-laws, etc.
Identify agencies promoting healthy family living

subtopics.name: Family Planning and Safe Motherhood
objectives: Explain the meaning and need for family planning
Describe birth control methods
Explain safe motherhood

subtopics.name: Population Education
objectives: Define population and population education
Describe the census and its problems
Compare small and large populations

topics.name: Emotional and Social Health
topics.content: The meaning and interrelationship between emotional health and social health, and their attributes, should be discussed. Candidates should be able to identify personal problems and proffer solutions, and state factors that promote mental health. Types, causes, prevention and management of mental ill health, and the importance of mental and social health, should be discussed.

subtopics.name: Interrelationship of Emotional and Social Health
objectives: Explain the interrelationship between emotional and social health

subtopics.name: Attributes of Emotional and Social Health
objectives: Define personality and personality traits
Identify personality problems and solutions

subtopics.name: Mental Health
objectives: Define mental health
Describe its promotion
Identify its types and prevention
Explain its importance

topics.name: Consumer Health Education
topics.content: The importance of checking label expiry dates on products before purchase should be highlighted. Various agencies promoting consumer health should be discussed, and the features of genuine products and services mentioned.

subtopics.name: Consumer Health Products and Services
objectives: Describe consumer health products and services

subtopics.name: Laws Protecting the Consumer
objectives: State the laws protecting the consumer

subtopics.name: Factors Influencing Choice of Consumer Products
objectives: Explain the factors influencing choice of consumer products: authenticity, cost, availability, accessibility and advertisement

subtopics.name: Consumer Health Care Services
objectives: Describe the various types of health services: traditional medicine, orthodox medicine and alternative methods of healing (acupuncture, yoga and faith healing)

subtopics.name: Quacks and Quackery
objectives: Define quacks and quackery and identify their types: mechanical, electrical, drug, cosmetic and medical quackery
State the dangers of quacks and quackery

subtopics.name: Health Insurance and Advertisement of Health Products and Services
objectives: Explain the meaning and importance of health insurance
Describe the state of health insurance
Discuss the advertisement of health products and consumer services

subtopics.name: Nostrum
objectives: Define nostrum and identify its types: health tonics, miracle substances, magic potions, amulets and talismans
State the reasons for avoiding nostrum
